doc.title: Billy Bauer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Touring with Herman: Army bases, a stripped plane and San Diego
summary: Travel by bus, train and a bare cargo plane with parachutes; in San Diego the band lived out of town to avoid servicemen.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: What was it like touring with Woody Herman? Was it mostly train or did you get cars that you traveled around the country in?

No we had bus and train. Later on when we did some Army bases again, one time they put us in a plane. These Army bases they would like — giving them a free concert or whatever. They put us in a plane. The plane was stripped — nothing in it. A big like it was a—

Yeah, but nothing in it. No windows in it. And they put the parachute on us and strapped us in. That was our seat. We just sat on the floor. And you could fall out. Well that was Woody. And another time out in California they took us into San Diego and we had to play the show for the servicemen. But we couldn’t live in San Diego. Because if you were a civilian you’d get beat up. So they shipped us 20 miles out on one of these coastal motels. They put the band there and picked us up and bring us to the back door to the concert stage, and they’d line up all soldiers on each side of us to protect us. They were afraid if we lived in San Diego we’d go out at night and being that we didn’t have any uniforms on, we’d get beat up.
Okay, they didn’t appreciate civilians. Yeah San Diego, there is a big military base there, right?
Yeah, yeah. Well that was an awful— but we played all of them, you know, for the soldiers. It was good. That was with Woody. And I did it with Abe, too Abe Lyman.
